delta.statement: line-local: the first span line `#[allow(clippy::missing_safety_doc)]` was removed; every remaining span line is identical. The `unsafe extern "C" fn` qualifier, signature, parameters, body `{ 0 }` and closing brace are unchanged, so no codegen, symbol, ABI or observable behaviour changes.

answers.a_safe_rust_can_cause_ub: No. The callback is a total function: the body is the literal `0`, it binds no argument (all parameters are `_`-prefixed), dereferences nothing, calls nothing and touches no global, thread-local or allocation. Every argument value -- including null, dangling, unaligned, or an arbitrary length -- returns 0 with no memory access, so there is no precondition a safe Rust caller could violate.
answers.b_all_unsafe_covered: Yes. The operation contains no unsafe block, call or dereference; the only `unsafe` is the `extern "C" fn` qualifier that names the C ABI boundary, and its precondition set is empty (`precondition_set: []`). The `# Safety` block now states exactly that, replacing the previous clippy allow.
answers.c_hidden_obligation: None. The callback is private and non-exported (`nm -D` on the admitted libcrypto.so.3 names no readbuffer symbol), is never address-taken outside its one method-table slot, and its only writer remains the static READBUFFER_METHOD slot. No new caller, alias, layout or lifetime obligation appears.
answers.d_load_bearing_control: Two controls ran here. (1) Firing control: the closure's content binding fired on these exact rows before this rebind -- evidence/closure-ssh-b83.json and closure-sshd-b83.json record 2 BLOCKED with `span-hash-mismatch` -- so the detector is not blind to a stale span, and it is the same predicate that must accept the rebound hash. (2) Behaviour control: the B67 public BIO probe `courts/phase25/rt_bio_readbuffer_control.c`, rebuilt against the b83 admitted install, PASSes (BIO_write=0 BIO_puts=0 pending 4->4 cache_unchanged), so the total-callback behaviour the empty precondition set relies on is observed at this candidate.
